Make the hub look like a professional product company site, with real pictures. Keep the current links, language toggle, dark mode and mobile layout.

1. Real screenshots: use your browser tooling (Playwright is in the project) to capture each live app at 1440x900 and save them as optimized WebP in public/shots/: https://paperrepro-aiid.atoms.world (home), https://paperrepro-aiid.atoms.world benchmark tab (click "Benchmark"), https://reprolite-aiid.pub.atoms.world, https://readingcompanion-aiid.pub.atoms.world, https://indexboard-aiid.pub.atoms.world/b/5dhum9j5h0, https://reprodesk-aiid.pub.atoms.world. If one fails, retry once, then use a clean placeholder frame with the app name. Commit the image files; do not hotlink.
2. Hero: put a large browser-frame mockup on the right showing the Paper Repro Agent screenshot, with two smaller overlapping frames (IndexBoard and Repro Lite) for depth. Subtle shadow, rounded corners, no stock photos.
3. A numbers strip under the hero, from our real results: "32 papers", "6 models compared", "281 benchmark runs", "~7 pt run-to-run noise measured", "5 live tools".
4. Tool cards: add the app screenshot at the top of each card (16:10, cropped from the top), keep the text and Open button.
5. "How a check works" section: five steps in a row with simple line icons (lucide): Read the paper, Fix the tolerance before running, Write and run code, Clean re-run from scratch, Audit and verdict. One sentence each.
6. "Example result" section: a card showing a real run: Isolation Forest, paper only, reported 0.85 AUC, reproduced 0.849 in a clean re-run, inside the ±0.03 band set before running, 23 min, about ¥0.53. Link "See the recorded run" to https://paperrepro-aiid.atoms.world.
7. "Shared, safe back end" section: three short points (key stays on the server behind a rate-limited gateway, agent code runs in the visitor's browser, everything bilingual), with icons.
8. Footer: team line (Group 1, Tsinghua SIGS AIID capstone, partners DeepWisdom and StepFun), links to all five tools.
Keep it calm and editorial: blue and neutral palette, serif headings, generous spacing, no emoji, no fake testimonials, no invented numbers beyond the ones above. English and Chinese for every new text. Check 390px has no horizontal scroll.
I'll start by checking whether Playwright and a browser binary are available for capturing the screenshots.
Python Playwright and Pillow are both installed, so I'll write a capture script that saves each screenshot as WebP, retries once, and falls back to a placeholder frame.
All six screenshots captured on the first attempt. Next I'm writing the bilingual content, a reusable browser-frame component, and the redesigned page.
Lint and build pass. You asked me to check for horizontal scroll at 390px, so I'll measure that on the built site in a headless browser, in both languages.
The page has no horizontal scroll at 390px in English or Chinese, so next I'll run the visual check.
The check reported blank image areas, so I'll test whether the captured screenshots are actually empty or whether lazy loading kept them from appearing.
The screenshots do contain real content, so the blank areas were most likely lazy-loaded images that hadn't loaded yet. I'll load the screenshots eagerly, update the notes, and re-validate.

The hub now looks like a product company site, with real screenshots of your apps. Links, the language toggle, dark mode and the mobile layout all still work. Lint and the build pass, and a visual check showed every section in place.

**What's new on the page:**
- **Screenshots:** I captured all six live pages at 1440×900, including the Paper Repro Agent Benchmark tab after clicking "Benchmark". Each worked on the first try, so no placeholder frames were needed. They're saved as WebP files of about 40–70 KB in `public/shots/` and served from the site, not hotlinked.
- **Hero:** a large browser frame with the Paper Repro Agent screenshot on the right, plus smaller overlapping Repro Lite and IndexBoard frames. Rounded corners and a soft shadow, no stock photos.
- **Numbers strip:** only your five numbers: 32 papers, 6 models compared, 281 benchmark runs, ~7 pt run-to-run noise, 5 live tools.
- **Tool cards:** each card has its screenshot on top (16:10, cropped from the top), with the text and Open button unchanged.
- **New sections:**
  - "How a check works": five steps with line icons.
  - "Example result": the Isolation Forest run (0.85 reported, 0.849 reproduced, inside ±0.03, 23 min, about ¥0.53). It has a small chart of the band, the "See the recorded run" link, and the Benchmark screenshot.
  - "Shared, safe back end": three points with icons.
- **Footer:** team line, DeepWisdom and StepFun as partners, and links to all five tools.

There's no horizontal scroll at 390px in English or Chinese. I measured this on the built site in a headless browser. Every new piece of text has a Chinese version.

**Please check:**
- **Wording I wrote:** you gave the step titles and short points, but I wrote the one-sentence explanations under each "How a check works" step and each back-end point. I also added a label to the example card that says the result is inside the band. Please check these against how your tools actually work.
- **Screenshots aren't committed:** the project's git folder is read-only here, so the commit failed. The image files are saved in the project and will go out when you publish. If an app's look changes, I can re-run the capture script (`scripts/capture_shots.py`) to refresh them.
- **Demo button:** "Watch the demo" still opens Paper Repro Agent. Send me a real demo link if you have one.

You can review it in App Viewer, then click Publish to update the live site.
The redesign is done, so I'm writing up the results.

# Project Summary
Repro Suite is a bilingual hub for discovering and opening five research-reproducibility tools. Its static pages describe each tool and its intended audience, with links that open in new tabs. The hub also includes language and theme controls, plus a blog. It does not require a database or API keys.

# Project Module Description
- **Hub page:** Presents the tools, a hero section with “Explore the tools” and “Watch the demo” actions, and a credit line: “Built on Atoms by Group 1, Tsinghua SIGS AIID capstone.” The demo action opens Paper Repro Agent.
- **Tool directory:** Five cards with English and Chinese descriptions and audience labels:
  - **Paper Repro Agent:** Checks whether a paper’s headline number reproduces by reading, setting tolerance, writing code, rerunning clean, and auditing. For researchers and reviewers.
  - **Repro Lite:** Checks one claim in about 40 seconds using an agent that runs Python in the browser. For students and readers seeking a quick check.
  - **Reading Companion:** Reads arXiv papers with users, saves quoted notes, cites claims, and marks what it could not verify. For anyone reading papers outside their field.
  - **IndexBoard:** Turns results or a sentence into a leaderboard with intervals and ties; AI can build the board and retrieve live model data. For evaluation teams and anyone comparing models.
  - **Repro Desk:** Offers a human-checked reproduction request for a paper as a free pilot. For labs and authors.
- **Language and theme controls:** English/Chinese and light/dark toggles; preferences are remembered between visits.
- **Blog:** Blog index and article pages, Markdown rendering, and prerendering support.
- **Shared UI:** Reusable components and hooks for navigation, forms, dialogs, notifications, and responsive layouts.

# Directory Tree
```text
app/frontend/
├── .mgx/config.yaml                 # Project tooling configuration
├── DESIGN.md                        # Design guidance
├── README.md                        # Frontend setup notes
├── components.json                  # UI component configuration
├── eslint.config.js                 # ESLint configuration
├── index.html                       # HTML entry template
├── package.json                     # Dependencies and npm scripts
├── playwright.config.ts             # Playwright configuration
├── plugins/                         # Development safeguards and tests
├── postcss.config.js                # PostCSS configuration
├── prerender/                       # Blog prerendering and sitemap utilities
├── public/                          # Favicon and crawler instructions
├── site.config.json                 # Site configuration
├── src/
│   ├── App.tsx                       # App root and route setup
│   ├── App.css                       # App-level styles
│   ├── blog-routes.tsx               # Blog route definitions
│   ├── index.css                     # Global styles and theme tokens
│   ├── main.tsx                      # React entry point
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── blog/                     # Blog article layout and Markdown renderer
│   │   └── ui/                       # Reusable interface components
│   ├── hooks/                        # Mobile viewport and toast hooks
│   ├── lib/
│   │   ├── api.ts                    # API utilities
│   │   ├── blog.ts                   # Blog data helpers
│   │   ├── config.ts                 # Configuration helpers
│   │   ├── content.ts                # Static tool content and translations
│   │   └── utils.ts                  # Shared utilities
│   ├── pages/
│   │   ├── AuthCallback.tsx          # Authentication callback page
│   │   ├── AuthError.tsx             # Authentication error page
│   │   ├── Index.tsx                 # Main hub page and tool cards
│   │   └── blog/                     # Blog index and post pages
│   └── vite-env.d.ts                 # Vite type declarations
├── tailwind.config.ts                # Tailwind CSS configuration
├── template_config.json              # Template settings
├── tsconfig*.json                    # TypeScript configurations
└── vite.config.ts                    # Vite configuration
```

# File Description Inventory
- `src/lib/content.ts`: Static tool descriptions, audience labels, and bilingual content.
- `src/pages/Index.tsx`: Hub hero, credit line, tool cards, language and theme controls.
- `src/App.tsx`, `src/main.tsx`: Application routing and entry point.
- `src/index.css`, `src/App.css`: Global design tokens and application styles.
- `src/pages/blog/`, `src/components/blog/`, `src/blog-routes.tsx`: Blog pages, article rendering, and routes.
- `prerender/`: Blog prerendering, sitemap generation, and helpers.
- `src/components/ui/`: Reusable interface components.
- `src/lib/`: Content, configuration, blog, API, and utility helpers.
- `plugins/`: Development safeguards and tests.
- Root configuration files: Build, lint, styling, type-checking, and browser-test configuration.

# Technology Stack
- React and TypeScript
- Vite
- Tailwind CSS and PostCSS
- Reusable component-based UI
- Playwright and ESLint
- Static site content; no database or API keys required

# Usage
From the frontend directory, install dependencies and start the development server:
```bash
cd app/frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Run checks and build:
```bash
npm run lint
npm run build
```
